legacy_cells.B: Multi-Task TabGraphSyn: Graph-Based Synthetic EHR Generation with Improved Quality-Privacy Trade-offs for Opioid Use Disorder Prediction
legacy_cells.C: Mohammad Arif Ul Alam; Sophia Shalhout
legacy_cells.I: 063_2026_Multi-Task TabGraphSyn Graph-Based Synthetic EHR Generation with Improved Quality-Privacy Trade-offs for Opioid Use Disorder Prediction.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Opioid use disorder (OUD; opioid abuse and dependence)
legacy_cells.S: Whether synthetic EHR records preserve fidelity, privacy, and utility for downstream prediction of 180-day opioid abuse and opioid concept groups.
legacy_cells.T: NIH All of Us OUD cohort: 11,600 patients, including 2,746 cases and 8,854 matched controls.
legacy_cells.AI: Structured/tabular EHR and survey variables; aggregated clinical-history text sequences for conditions, drug exposures, laboratory measurements, and procedures, embedded with BioClinicalBERT
legacy_cells.AJ: Graph convolutional encoder (GCN); conditional VAE encoder and decoder implemented as multilayer perceptrons
legacy_cells.AM: Concatenation of structured features with four domain-specific BioClinicalBERT embeddings, followed by PCA dimensionality reduction
legacy_cells.AN: Median imputation for missing values; records with completely missing clinical history were removed
legacy_cells.BS: Synthetic tabular feature vectors decoded from latent vectors conditioned on graph embeddings; task-label tuples appended by bootstrap sampling
legacy_cells.BT: MultiOutputClassifier with logistic-regression base learners for the three downstream prediction tasks
legacy_cells.BV: GCN graph-smoothness loss plus embedding-norm regularization; CVAE reconstruction loss plus KL-divergence regularization
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): Results on the NIH All of Us dataset show that TabGraphSyn achieves a stronger overall utility-privacy balance, outperforming MIIC in most headline metrics, including higher synthetic multi-task ROC-AUC (0.5278 vs 0.4932), MetaQPS (AM: 0.0215 vs 0.0115; HM: 0.0391 vs 0.0223), while slightly underperforming in macro F1 (0.2321 vs 0.2840).
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–18: title/abstract and introduction (pp. 1–2); methods, cohort, feature engineering, graph/CVAE architecture, training, and generation (pp. 2–10); experiments and metrics (pp. 10–14); results and Tables 1–2 (pp. 14–16); limitations and future directions (p. 17); remaining references (pp. 17–18). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left untouched. The implemented model generates static tabular records; its longitudinal histories are aggregated into feature representations, and temporal/event-sequence modeling is identified as future work, so no state transition or world-model capability is supported. Demonstrated results (Table 1, PDF p. 15) include synthetic macro ROC-AUC 0.5278 ± 0.0285 vs 0.4932 ± 0.0174 for MIIC-SDG, macro F1 0.2321 ± 0.0173 vs 0.2840 ± 0.0115, and MetaQPS-AM 0.0215 ± 0.0150 vs 0.0115 ± 0.0099. These measured metrics are reported separately from the authors’ overall favorable utility-privacy interpretation. Tables 1–2 were text-extracted legibly; no unreadable-table issue noted.
